text.p: Lazard Freres & Co. on Wednesday increased its rating on Mexican retailer Cifra SA de CV to buy from hold in the wake of last week's announcement of a far-reaching transaction between Cifra and Wal-Mart.

--Analysts Curtis Bulter and Kristina M. Salen said in a report that the proposed deal "will give control of the company (Cifra) to Wal-Mart, which is likely to infuse a more growth-oriented approach and add to financial flexibility."
--The two companies announced last week that Wal-Mart and Cifra, which is Mexico's largest retailer, would merge joint venture projects in Mexico, with Wal-Mart taking over control of the company.
--Butler and Salen said the deal "in essence gives Mexico's largest and most profitable self-service retailer the one important element it lacked: growth."
--The Lazard Freres analysts said "this combination of high profitability and higher growth" will benefit shareholders over the medium to long term.
--Also, Wal-Mart's plans to buy a portion of the Cifra voting shares "at a substantial premium ... creates an attractive arbitrage opportunity for investors concerned about near-term dilution."
